A complete, opinionated field manual: installing Python without wrecking your Linux box, configuring it like an adult, understanding why PEP 668 exists, writing code that survives contact with hostile input, choosing libraries by objective, and operating the result in production. Fifteen gated levels. Every gate must be passed before the next one opens. Current stable Python 3.15.0 released 2026-10-09 Also supported 3.14 · 3.13 · 3.12 · 3.11 3.10 reached EOL 2026-10-01 Audience Beginners → operators Linux-first, cross-platform Prereqs A terminal No prior Python assumed Begin at Level 00 → Continue where I left off Jump to references How the gate works Levels unlock in order. Each ends with a knowledge check; you need all questions correct to pass. Wrong answers are explained — the explanation is the actual lesson, so read it before retrying. Progress is stored locally in your browser, and nothing is sent anywhere. This page is one HTML file with zero external requests; all links open documentation in a new tab. Level 00 Orientation not started ~14 min What Python actually is (and what it is not) Most Python damage happens before the first line of code: wrong interpreter, wrong environment, wrong expectations. Before touching an installer, build the mental model. Python is a language specification plus a reference implementation. CPython — the one you get from python.org , your distro, or uv — compiles your source to bytecode and executes it on a virtual machine. That distinction explains almost every confusing error message you will meet. The five things that exist on disk When you install "Python", you are really installing a layout. Learn it once and environment bugs stop being mysterious. python -m sysconfig | head -40 prints the real paths for the interpreter you are running. Interpreter anatomy Thing Typical Linux path What it means python3 /usr/bin/python3 The executable (often a symlink). Its version can differ from every other Python on the box. stdlib /usr/lib/python3.13/ Batteries included: json , pathlib , ssl , sqlite3 . Owned by the OS or installer. site-packages …/site-packages/ Third-party packages. This is the directory virtual environments exist to isolate. scripts/bin ~/.local/bin , .venv/bin Console entry points ( pytest , ruff ). Must be on PATH to be callable by name. config ~/.config/pip/pip.conf Index URLs, caches, credentials. A wrong setting here breaks every install silently. Four layers, one process Python code lives in a stack of layers. Bugs that look like "Python is broken" are nearly always a mismatch between two adjacent layers. Language — syntax and semantics. Versioned by minor release (3.12, 3.13, 3.14, 3.15). New syntax can be unavailable on older interpreters, which is why requires-python exists. Standard library — ships with the interpreter, has the same version number, and is not installable via pip. Never pip install json ; that package name is a squatter. Third-party packages — installed into a site-packages directory, resolved by sys.path order. Your project — source code plus a declaration of which of the above it needs. bash · confirm what you are actually running copy python3 -VV # e.g. Python 3.13.7 (main, ...) [GCC 14.2.0] which -a python3 python # every Python on PATH, in resolution order python3 -c 'import sys; print(sys.executable); print(sys.prefix); print(sys.path)' That last command is the single most useful diagnostic in Python. sys.executable tells you which binary runs; sys.prefix tells you which environment it belongs to; sys.path tells you where imports will look, first match wins. If a package "is installed but cannot be imported", these three lines answer the question in seconds. Bad decision #0 — "Python is installed, so I can pip install anything" There are usually three or more Pythons on a modern Linux machine: the OS one ( /usr/bin/python3 ), a Homebrew or pyenv one, and one inside each project. pip on your PATH may belong to none of the ones you run. This is the root cause of the classic "I installed requests but Python says ModuleNotFoundError" . The fix is not to reinstall — it is to stop calling bare pip . Use python -m pip , or better, activate the project environment first. Then pip cannot point at the wrong interpreter, because it is the interpreter. How this manual is meant to be read Each level assumes the previous ones. Level 01–03 (install, configure, environments) are the foundation: skipping them is why so many tutorials fail on a real machine. Levels 04–06 are the language and standard library. Levels 07–08 are where careers are made — security and testing. Levels 09–11 cover the ecosystem, packaging, and the anti-patterns gallery. Levels 12–14 are operations, performance, and long-term maintenance. Every section ends with a References block pointing at documentation deeper than this page. Read at least one primary source per level; the manual is a map, not a replacement for the territory. There are five legitimate strategies with different blast radii. Choosing the wrong one is how people end up with a broken desktop and a stack of Stack Overflow tabs. First, a rule that will save you hours: never let a project depend on the operating system's Python . Your distro uses Python for system tooling — package managers, drivers, desktop utilities. Treat /usr/bin/python3 as read-only infrastructure and install your own interpreter for your own work. Choose your strategy Installation strategies compared Strategy Best for Cost / risk OS packages apt , dnf , pacman Running distro tooling; quickly getting a Python for small scripts; servers with a strict "no unmanaged software" policy. Older version, patched by the distro, externally managed (PEP 668). You cannot pip-install into it. pyenv Needing several CPython versions per user; reproducing an old project; testing against 3.11–3.15. Compiles from source: needs build deps and ~5–15 min per version. Shims can confuse editors. uv python install The modern default for developer machines and CI. Fast, per-user, no root, no compile step. One more tool to learn; standalone builds may lag a patch release by days. Official installer (.pkg / .exe) Windows and macOS desktops, especially beginners; no compiler toolchain available. Manual upgrades; on Windows the PATH checkbox and the Microsoft Store alias are a classic trap. Containers python:3.13-slim Anything deployed; reproducible CI; "works on my machine" elimination. Not for day-to-day editing unless you wire volumes; image size and base-image patching are your job. Why "just use the latest" is not the whole answer Python's annual release cadence (October) means a brand-new minor version is often not yet supported by every C-extension you depend on. For production, the pragmatic choice in late 2026 is the newest version that your dependency set publishes wheels for — usually 3.13 or 3.14, moving to 3.15 after a few months. For learning, use the latest stable. Check the support table before you commit: 3.10 went end-of-life on 2026-10-01 and no longer receives security fixes. Linux: the distro route Debian and Ubuntu ship a solid CPython but split it across packages. The interpreter alone cannot create virtual environments — you need the venv module package, and pip is often absent by design. bash · Debian 12/13, Ubuntu 24.04+ copy sudo apt update sudo apt install -y python3 python3-venv python3-pip python3-dev build-essential python3 -VV python3 -m venv --help >/dev/null && echo "venv OK" bash · Fedora / RHEL family copy sudo dnf install -y python3 python3-pip python3-devel gcc redhat-rpm-config # Versioned interpreters are separate packages, e.g.: sudo dnf install -y python3.13 python3.13-pip bash · Arch copy sudo pacman -S --needed python python-pip # Arch tracks the latest release; do not partial-upgrade around it. On Ubuntu, newer interpreters are available from the deadsnakes PPA ( sudo add-apt-repository ppa:deadsnakes/ppa ). It is a genuine convenience, but the maintainers are explicit that timely security updates are not guaranteed . That is fine for a scratch machine and a poor default for production. Prefer uv , pyenv , or building from source when you need a version the distro does not ship. Linux: the per-user route with uv uv installs standalone CPython builds (from the python-build-standalone project) into your home directory. No root, no compilation, no system changes. bash · uv (Astral) copy curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh # review the script first on servers uv python install 3.14 # downloads a standalone build uv python list # available + installed uv python find 3.14 # absolute path to the interpreter uv python pin 3.14 # writes .python-version for this project Piping curl into sh Convenient, and a supply-chain habit worth breaking. For anything you care about, download the script, read it, verify the checksum/signature where the project provides one, then run it. The same applies to installers from any vendor — including Python-adjacent tooling. "It's from a well-known project" is not verification; a compromised release is still a release. Linux: pyenv, when you need exact versions bash · pyenv from source copy # Build dependencies (Debian/Ubuntu) sudo apt install -y make build-essential libssl-dev zlib1g-dev \ libbz2-dev libreadline-dev libsqlite3-dev libffi-dev liblzma-dev \ libncursesw5-dev xz-utils tk-dev libgdbm-dev uuid-dev curl -fsSL https://pyenv.run | bash # then add to ~/.bashrc as printed by the installer exec "$SHELL" -l pyenv install 3.13.7 pyenv versions pyenv global 3.13.7 # default for your user pyenv local 3.12.11 # per-directory override, writes .python-version The classic pyenv failure is a silently missing libsqlite3-dev or libssl-dev : the build succeeds, then import sqlite3 or HTTPS fails. Always run the verification block below after any source build. On Debian/Ubuntu you can alternatively use the maintained python-build-standalone builds that uv and pyenv can consume. Windows: the installer and the Store trap Download the Windows installer from python.org/downloads/windows . Avoid third-party "Python bundles". Tick Add python.exe to PATH on the first screen. If you miss it, re-run the installer and choose Modify rather than reinstalling blindly. Prefer the per-user install unless you have a reason; it avoids UAC-admin surprises with pip. Use the py launcher ( py -0p lists installed versions, py -3.13 -m venv .venv selects one). Bad decision — the Microsoft Store stub named python.exe Windows ships a zero-byte execution alias at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\python.exe that opens the Store. If it comes first on PATH , running python launches a shop instead of an interpreter, and some tools report "Python was not found". Fix it in Settings → Apps → Advanced app settings → App execution aliases by disabling the python.exe and python3.exe aliases, then ensure your real install's Scripts and root directory precede WindowsApps on PATH . Deleting the alias file directly is a worse idea — an update may recreate it. macOS: two good options bash · Homebrew vs official installer copy brew install python@3.14 # installs to /opt/homebrew (Apple Silicon) brew link --overwrite python@3.14 python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate # Or: the universal2 installer from python.org (includes Tcl/Tk, IDLE, certifi bundle) # Never use the system /usr/bin/python3 for project work: Apple ships it for Xcode tooling. Homebrew's Python is externally managed too: brew install for tools, virtual environments for libraries. Do not pip install into it, and do not sudo a Homebrew Python. Containers: the reproducibility escape hatch bash · Docker copy docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD":/app -w /app python:3.14-slim bash # inside: python -VV pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt Pin the full image tag or digest ( python:3.14.0-slim-bookworm , or better a @sha256:… digest) for reproducibility. python:latest is a moving target and will break your build on a random Tuesday. Verify the install like you mean it Version output alone proves nothing: a Python can be present but unable to create environments, verify TLS certificates, or import its own standard library modules. Run the full check. bash · post-install smoke test copy python3 -VV python3 -c "import sys, ssl, sqlite3, zlib, lzma, ctypes, hashlib; print(sys.executable); print(ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION); print(sqlite3.sqlite_version)" python3 -m venv /tmp/pycheck && /tmp/pycheck/bin/python -m pip --version && rm -rf /tmp/pycheck python3 -c "import urllib.request; print(urllib.request.urlopen('https://pypi.org', timeout=5).status)" If the HTTPS request fails with a certificate error, you have a broken CA bundle (common with hand-built Pythons and minimal containers) — fix the bundle rather than reaching for verify=False . If venv fails on Debian/Ubuntu, install python3-venv . If import sqlite3 fails, the interpreter was compiled without SQLite headers. Version management policy that scales Dev machine Latest stable + one older Run 3.14/3.15 for new work, keep 3.12 or 3.13 installed so you can reproduce bug reports. uv python install 3.13 3.14 costs a few hundred MB and saves days. CI Matrix, not guesswork Test the oldest version your requires-python allows and the newest stable. A matrix of five versions catches syntax and typing regressions early. Production One pinned minor Pin the exact patch in the image ( 3.13.7-slim ) and rebuild monthly for security patches. Upgrade minors deliberately, not automatically. Bad decision — building with sudo make install Running ./configure && sudo make install overwrites /usr/local/bin/python3 and its stdlib, which sits ahead of the distro's Python on PATH . System tools that expect the distro build can then break in ways that are hard to trace, and uninstalling is genuinely painful (no package record). If you must build from source, use make altinstall and a --prefix inside your home directory, or use pyenv/uv, which do exactly that for you. The five minutes you save are repaid with interest the first time apt misbehaves. This level is the difference between an interpreter you fight and one that behaves. Configuration happens at three scopes: the shell (PATH and exported variables), the interpreter ( site , .pth files, user site), and tooling (pip config, editor, git hooks). Get the order right and everything else composes. 1. PATH: the only config most people need Programs are found through PATH , left to right. Console scripts installed with pip --user and pipx land in ~/.local/bin (Linux/macOS) or %APPDATA%\Python\Python3xx\Scripts (Windows). If that directory is missing from PATH , the install succeeds and the command "does not exist". bash · make user scripts visible (Linux/macOS) copy echo "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -E '\.local/bin|\.venv|pyenv' # Append once, in ~/.profile for POSIX shells, or ~/.zshrc / ~/.bashrc for interactive shells: echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.profile exec "$SHELL" -l command -v pytest ruff uv pipx Which file: .bashrc, .profile, .zshrc? ~/.bashrc runs for interactive non-login shells; ~/.profile runs for login shells (and is read by most display managers); zsh uses ~/.zshrc + ~/.zprofile . GUI applications and systemd services often start without your interactive shell config, so a PATH that works in the terminal can still be missing under systemd. That is why services should call interpreters by absolute path (see Level 13), not rely on PATH . Bad decision — alias python=python3 and alias pip=pip3 It feels harmless. It is not: aliases do not apply to scripts, cron, systemd, IDEs, or subprocess , so you get a machine that behaves one way interactively and another way in production. On Debian/Ubuntu, python is deliberately absent from the base system because Python 2-era tooling would silently pick it up. Worse, alias pip=pip3 hides which interpreter pip belongs to. The robust fix is to create a virtual environment and let python and pip both resolve inside .venv/bin . If you truly need a user-level python , use a symlink in ~/.local/bin pointing at a specific version and understand that every non-shell context will ignore it. 2. pip: configure it once, correctly pip reads configuration from three scopes — global ( /etc/pip.conf ), user ( ~/.config/pip/pip.conf ), and site ( .venv/pip.conf ) — plus PIP_* environment variables. Later scopes win, and command-line flags beat everything. Inspect before editing: bash · pip configuration copy python3 -m pip config debug # every file considered, and its values python3 -m pip config list python3 -m pip --version # confirm which pip, from which environment python3 -m pip cache dir # where wheels are cached ini · ~/.config/pip/pip.conf copy [global] # Only change these if your organisation actually runs a mirror. # index-url = https://pypi.org/simple timeout = 20 retries = 3 disable-pip-version-check = true [install] # Fail loudly instead of silently drifting when a version is yanked. prefer-binary = true Bad decision — trusted-host as a permanent fix Adding trusted-host or --trusted-host disables TLS certificate verification for that index. People add it to silence corporate-proxy errors and then forget it exists; every package they install afterwards is trivially interceptable. The correct fixes are: install your organisation's CA certificate into the system trust store, point pip at it with cert = /path/ca.pem , or configure the proxy in pip.conf . If you inherit a machine with trusted-host set, treat it as a security finding. 3. The environment variables that matter Python honours a set of PYTHON* variables at startup. A few are useful; several are dangerous because they change behaviour for every program you run. Use python -X option or -E / -I in scripts to ignore the environment entirely. Selected PYTHON* environment variables Variable Effect Verdict PYTHONPATH Prepends directories to sys.path . Avoid. Shadowing risk; use installed packages or uv run . PYTHONSTARTUP Script executed by the interactive interpreter only. Safe for conveniences, never for application logic. PYTHONDEVMODE Enables development mode: extra warnings, debug hooks. Good in CI ( PYTHONDEVMODE=1 ). PYTHONWARNINGS Warning filters, e.g. error to turn warnings into exceptions. Useful in tests; do not rely on it in production. PYTHONSAFEPATH Like -P : do not prepend the script's directory / CWD. Good hardening for tools run on untrusted trees. PYTHONNOUSERSITE Ignores

racismo: O Racismo é mais do que Palavras Comparativas Ser "Preto" é ser objectivado e limitado a uma cor só, sem forma, sem irregularidades da cor, tão ou mais escura do que a cor da sombra de um objecto estático ou em movimento ou até, um ser que está parado ou em movimento. Ser "preto" poderá ser ofensivo nessa noção de que só a cor preta é preta e ser "preto" é ser cor sem incluir a forma. Ser "branco" é igual e ser "amarelo" também. É limitar e simplificar o Ser a algo tão básico quanto uma cor. Mas o Racismo não é uma comparação, pois as comparações servem a simplificação das objectivações. Um Leão é um animal selvagem e quando alguém diz que outra pessoa parece "um leão", estará também a fazer uma comparação irreal e falsa, pois há vários aspectos físicos e comportamentais que se diferenciam entre um leão e uma pessoa. O mesmo acontece com a expressão que define uma pessoa de "Macaco". Existe um programa na Internet (no YouTube) chamado "O Lado Negro da Força", que se dedica não só a falar da cultura Africana, mas também a referir e a discutir problemas associados ao Racismo, sendo que a pessoa que lidera o programa, tenta fazer a relação entre a expressão de "macaco" com racismo, por causa de uma espécie de semelhança visual, que é bem irreal, sendo que os considerados agressores da história, usavam esta expressão para definir pessoas de origem africana, ficando assim na memória das pessoas africanas, como uma expressão que representa Racismo. A meu ver, este tipo de relação deveria ser combatida via a vontade de vencer e não deveria ser alimentada, via a vontade de ser vítima do que é puramente subjectivo. Nenhuma pessoa é mais do que uma pessoa e caso uma qualquer comparação tente definir uma pessoa como algo mais além de ser uma pessoa, essa definição será falsa, ou poderá ser unicamente subjectiva e criativa. Mesmo entendendo o sofrimento de quem foi alvo da expressão que ofende, deverei lembrar o poder da mente, que tem a capacidade de negar o Verbo ou até dar-lhe um novo sentido e signficado. Nasci numa cultura que usa comparações desde sempre e mesmo que essa técnica tenha sido combatida e objectivada como a origem do " Bulling ", a meu ver, mesmo tendo sido vítima dessa técnica, não é "bulling" nem creio que a técnica seja ofensiva, mas verdadeiramente educativa. Fazendo referência a um artigo escrito por mim com o nome de Uma Lição Divína , num outro blog no qual escrevo com menos regularidade, pois esta plataforma foi usada por mim antes de ter um site dedicado e gerido por mim, tento descrever a importância deste método linguístico, que está entranhado na literatura Religiosa, Espiritual, Infantil, Fantástica e até do foro Cientifico, pois é na validação da informação que somos capazes de verificar a vericidade de uma "verdade", encriminalizar o uso desta técnica, seria um atentado à eliminação da criatividade, da unicidade cultural dos povos e como tal, um atentado à liberdade. O Racismo é mais do que palavras. O Racismo é um comportamento físico que ataca fisicamente alguém, independentemente da sua origem ou cor, aplicando punições físicas e nada subjectivas (tal como as usadas pela língua em forma de comparações), tal como o uso da Violência Física. Se as palavras magoam, significa que somos capazes de pensar, pois até as palavras que não focam o nosso ser, podem produzir dor, tal como ver injustiças que outras pessoas são alvo. Por exemplo, actualmente quando vejo notícias de padres que violam crianças ou que declaram afirmações tais como "mais vale violar uma criança do que usar técnicas de masturbação", produz em mim uma dor e tanto faz qual a cor ora do padre ora da criança. A dor aparece via a consciência e sabendo que todos/as temos a Liberdade de nos opõr e negar as afirmações dos outros, a minha dor aumenta quando não vejo respostas que negam, mas que reafirmam esse tipo de injustiças que acontecem há mais de 20 séculos. Ser Leão é visto como uma comparação que demonstra "Coragem", sendo que também poderá ter como objectivo descrever esse comportamento injusto das feras que vitimizam seres pacíficos. São os Reis da Selva é o que alguns acreditam e por isso, os Reis tornaram-se seres impiedosos e injustos. Ser-se Macaco é visto como uma comparação que demonstra "ser-se infantil", sendo que também poderá ter como objectivo descrever alguém que faz muito barulho, quando os perigos estão à espreita. Os Macacos não são os Reis da Selva, mas lá ajudam que a selva não seja totalmente injusta para os mais desatentos. Ser-se infantil também é obra de quem é criativo, pois ser silêncioso é técnica de quem caça e não de quem nos poderá fazer rir ou até ensinar a pensar. É sempre importante saber pensar e questionar. Só quem não questiona é que é incapaz de lidar com a subjectividade, tornando-a tão objectiva e tão concreta que poderiamos acreditar que é palpável, quando na verdade é impossível definir os seus contornos, o seu volume e a sua cor. recycling: Monkey Blog · Second Lives Home EN PT Second lives · a manual in seventeen parts Nothing Is Garbage A bin is a decision someone else already made for you. This manual takes it back: what kitchen scraps, garden clippings, old clothes, jars, tins, pallets and dead electronics can become instead — with the recipes, the numbers, the traps and the sources, for a household, a garden, or a small business. Seventeen parts 75+ second lives Bin audit Compost calculator From waste to income Sources Start with my own bin Part 03: one week, a kitchen scale, and a number instead of a feeling. I want to use the scraps tonight Part 04: five things to do with peels, stale bread and coffee before they become a smell. I have a garden and a compost problem Part 05: the carbon/nitrogen balance, with a calculator that says how many litres to add. I want this to pay Part 13: repair, upcycling, compost and workshops — what people actually charge for. 01 The rule that changes everything Waste is not a property of an object. It is the moment someone stops imagining a use for it. That is good news, because imagination is cheap — and the order in which you apply it decides whether you are solving a problem or just moving it. Refuse — the only free option The bag, the straw, the second plastic tray, the free T-shirt at an event. Every object refused costs nothing to store, sort, clean or feel guilty about. This is the only rung with no downstream work. Reduce — use less of it, for longer A bigger jar of yoghurt, a refill bottle, a repair instead of a replacement. Reduction is boring and it is where most of the kilos actually disappear. Reuse and repair — the interesting middle Jars, crates, clothes, furniture, electronics. This manual lives here: the second life that keeps the material in service without melting it down. Rot — let biology do the work Food scraps and garden clippings are not waste, they are next year's soil. Composting is the cheapest transformation available to a household, and the one most often skipped. Recycle — the last resort that looks like the first Recycling destroys the object to recover the material. It needs energy, clean streams and a market. It is good, and it is fourth best — which is why a page about it should not start there. What you gain Money that stays in the house: a jar, a crate and a repaired lamp are things you no longer buy. Better bins: less smell, fewer flies, no liquid at the bottom, half the volume. Skills that transfer — cutting, sewing, composting, wiring a plug are the same skills at 60 as at 6. A garden that feeds itself instead of importing bags of soil. A reason to know your neighbours: the person with pallets, the café with buckets, the man who fixes toasters. What it costs Time, and the honest admission that ten minutes of labour can be worth less than a €2 object. Storage: the fatal temptation is a garage full of "someday". Every project needs a deadline or it is hoarding with better vocabulary. Standards: some second lives are not safe — food contact, children's toys, electrical work, anything structural. Aesthetic risk: visible mending is beautiful, a shelf made of three different woods is a shelf. The uncomfortable part: recycling is an industry with losses, and much of what you sort is burned or shipped. The scale, in four numbers. The average person in the EU generated 517 kg of municipal waste in 2024, and 48 % of it was recycled or composted. Biowaste is the single largest fraction of that bin at 28.8 % — food and garden waste, the part a household can transform without any industry at all. Globally, 1.05 billion tonnes of food were wasted in 2022, about 19 % of everything available to consumers, and food loss and waste produce 8–10 % of greenhouse-gas emissions. You cannot compost your way out of a supply chain. You can, however, remove a third of your own bin and half its smell this month. 02 Read the bin: eight materials, eight futures Every object is a material wearing a shape. Identify the material and the options appear — and so do the exclusions, which matter more. What each family wants to become, and where the second life stops being a good idea Family Typical pieces Best second life Where it stops The three questions before you keep anything A house is not a warehouse. Answer all three out loud, because a "maybe" is a no. Do I have a use, today? Not a use in the abstract: this shelf, this window, this person's birthday. Do I have the other half? A jar without a lid, a lamp without a cable, a frame without glass — the missing part is the project. Is it safe for that use? Food, children, heat, electricity and load-bearing are the five things you cannot improvise. 03 Audit your own bin Guilt is a bad measuring instrument. One week, one kitchen scale, five numbers — and you will know exactly which habit is worth changing, instead of changing all of them badly. People in the household Food and garden waste (kg per week) Plastic and metal packaging (kg per week) Paper and cardboard (kg per week) Glass (kg per week) Textiles and other (kg per week) Total / week — Per person / year — Could rot — Could be recycled — Still mixed — How to read the result The EU average is 517 kg per person per year. Under 300 means you are already unusual; over 600 means volume, not guilt, is the place to start. But the number that matters is the third one: the organic share is the only stream a household can process at home, without markets, trucks or a single kilowatt-hour. if organic wins Build the compost, then the garden A balcony bokashi bin handles 15 litres a month and takes no space. A worm bin handles a family's peels, and gives back the only fertiliser you will need for pots. if packaging wins Change the shop, not the bin Packaging is decided at the shelf. Two refill stops, one bigger format and a market with loose produce do more than a year of folding cartons perfectly. if textiles win Open a repair basket A box with needle, thread, patches and a spare button turns "I have nothing to wear" into twenty minutes. The rest becomes rags, then wicks, then compost-adjacent dust. 04 The kitchen: five lives before the bin A kitchen throws away food, water and packaging in the same gesture. These five habits catch the first two, cost nothing, and are the ones people keep doing after the novelty wears off. 20 minutes + 2 weeks · €0 Citrus-peel vinegar cleaner The peels you were going to bin become a degreaser strong enough for the stove. Peels of 3–4 oranges, lemons or limes 1 L of white vinegar (the cheap one) A jar with a lid Pack the peels into the jar and cover with vinegar. Leave it two weeks in a cupboard, shaking when you remember. Strain, keep the liquid, dilute half and half with water for surfaces. Never on marble, limestone or unsealed stone — the acid eats the surface. Never mixed with bleach. 5 minutes · 1–3 weeks Regrow from the end Spring onion, leek, celery, lettuce hearts and carrot tops will push new leaves from a centimetre of water. OdicforceSounds Em Português Catorze capítulos Pacífico e legal ✦ O que este documento não é Não é mais um manual de manifestações. Esses já existem neste arquivo e fazem bem o seu trabalho: Manifestações ensina os doze passos de uma marcha, ACT-101 ensina a engenharia de uma campanha. Este documento faz a pergunta que vem antes de todas as táticas e que quase ninguém escreve. Porque é que quase todas as revoltas morrem ao terceiro dia? Não por falta de razão. Não por falta de raiva. Morrem porque foram desenhadas como um acontecimento — e um acontecimento acaba. O que dura não é o grito: é a estrutura que fica depois de o grito passar. A regra deste texto Nada aqui pede que sejas herói. Tudo aqui pede que sejas útil durante mais tempo do que a paciência de quem te quer ver calado. ◉ O diagnóstico em cinco linhas O poder de 2026 não tem cara. Tem cinco caras parciais, e cada uma sozinha parece suportável. As cinco faces, e onde o arquivo as documenta Face Como se apresenta Onde está documentada A dívida Como oportunidade, depois como obrigação Economia Diabólica A casa Como escassez natural, nunca como decisão Proposta para a habitação Nenhuma destas faces cai com um empurrão. Todas cedem à mesma coisa: pressão mantida por gente que não se cansa ao mesmo tempo . É por isso que este documento não fala de coragem. Fala de desenho. ◒ A revolução-espetáculo falhou A forma dominante de revolta — o evento mediático, a multidão fotografada, a frase que circula — tem quatro defeitos fatais, e todos são de arquitectura. Mede-se em multidão. Uma praça cheia prova que havia gente. Não prova que havia acordo, nem que havia plano, nem que havia alguém para continuar amanhã. Vive de atenção. E a atenção é o recurso que o adversário controla melhor do que tu: basta-lhe mais um escândalo para o teu deixar de existir. Morre ao segundo dia. Porque não tem de onde tirar comida, dinheiro, apoio jurídico ou descanso — só tem indignação, e a indignação não paga rendas. Entrega o arquivo ao inimigo. Sem registo próprio, a história do que aconteceu é escrita por quem tem departamento de comunicação. Uma revolta que precisa de ser vista para existir é uma revolta que pode ser desligada. O que não pode ser desligado é o que já está a funcionar quando ninguém está a ver. ⚖ A tese: revolução é infraestrutura Há uma definição que sobrevive a todas as derrotas do século passado: uma revolução é a construção, antes da vitória, das coisas que a vitória deveria garantir. Não se conquista o que não se sabe manter. Então a pergunta deixa de ser «como derrubamos isto?» e passa a ser: o que é que já podemos pôr a funcionar sem pedir licença? Três coisas, e nenhuma delas se confisca de uma só vez: Cuidado Quem tem medo não participa. Comida, boleia, creche, apoio jurídico: a logística que transforma vontade em presença continuada. Arquivo Prova datada, verificável, publicada. O que não está registado não aconteceu — e o que não aconteceu não pode ser exigido. Tempo Ritmo. Reunião que se repete, caixa que se repõe, pessoa que é substituída antes de se gastar. A revolução é um calendário, não uma data. O que isto não é Não é uma promessa de que funciona. É a única forma que já se viu funcionar mais de uma vez sem se transformar naquilo contra o que lutava. ✕ Três recusas Antes de construir, é preciso recusar. As três recusas que se seguem são o que distingue uma estrutura de uma seita. O que se recusa, e porquê Recusa Como se disfarça O que custa A pureza «Quem não está connosco está contra nós.» Encolhe o grupo até ao tamanho de uma sala e transforma cada dúvida em expulsão. O líder «Alguém tem de falar pelos outros.» Cria um ponto único de pressão: quem quiser parar o movimento só precisa de parar uma pessoa. O segredo «É melhor que ninguém saiba.» Impede a correcção de erros e transforma a confiança em refém. As três recusas são desconfortáveis. A pureza dá energia, o líder dá voz, o segredo dá adrenalina. Mas todas as três trocam o futuro por uma noite boa — e a factura chega sempre na forma de um grupo que se odeia mais do que odeia o adversário. ⌂ Três construções Tudo o que este documento propõe cabe em três objectos físicos. Se não existirem, não há movimento: há conversa. 1 · A caixa comum Um envelope, uma conta partilhada, uma regra: três pessoas, duas assinaturas, um registo mensal público . Entra dinheiro de quem pode, sai para o que foi decidido em conjunto, e o extracto é lido em voz alta uma vez por mês. Sem isto, o grupo depende de quem tem dinheiro — e quem tem dinheiro acaba a decidir. 3 · A mesa comum Um sítio e uma hora fixos, todas as semanas, com a mesma ordem do dia: o que se passou, o que se decide, quem faz o quê até à próxima. A mesa é o que transforma um grupo de pessoas zangadas numa organização — e é a primeira coisa que se perde quando o grupo cresce depressa. Ordem de construção Caixa, arquivo, mesa — por esta ordem e nunca ao contrário. Um grupo com mesa e sem caixa discute bem e não faz nada. Um grupo com caixa e sem arquivo faz muito e não consegue provar nada. ⏱ O método dos trinta minutos A parte revolucionária é a mais entediante: uma prática diária de meia hora, dividida em três blocos de dez. Não porque meia hora muda o mundo — mas porque meia hora todos os dias muda quem a faz. rust-cli: Monkey Blog · Rust in the Shell Home EN PT Compiled tools · a manual in nineteen parts Rust in the Shell The tools that replaced half of the classic Unix commands were not written in C. The faster grep, the friendlier find, the cat with syntax colours, the prompt that draws itself, the fuzzy finder, the test runner — a surprising number of them are Rust binaries you install with one line. This manual is about the toolchain that compiles them, the register they come from, and thirty projects worth the wait. Nineteen parts Thirty crates MSRVs checked Install builder Route chooser Every repo linked I have never installed Rust Part 02: one script, one toolchain, and a compiler that is ready in four minutes. Show me the tools first Part 06: every crate with its version, MSRV, home page and what it does, plus the command for your machine. Just give me the command Part 03: cargo install, the pinned version, and where the binary lands. A build just failed Part 16: the messages that stop people, from a missing linker to an MSRV one release too new. 01 One register, three rules, a compiler you keep Rust is not a scripting language, and that is the first thing to accept: installing a tool means compiling it, and compiling it needs a compiler. In exchange there is one register (crates.io), one command ( cargo install ), and no runtime to keep alive afterwards — the result is a single executable that runs on a machine with nothing installed. These three rules are the whole of it; the rest of this manual is detail. One: rustup owns the compiler, cargo owns the crates rustup installs and switches toolchains; cargo builds and fetches crates. They are separate programs that agree on a directory. Do not install a second rustc from your distribution and expect the two to coexist politely: whichever comes first on PATH wins, and half the "this crate needs a newer Rust" reports are a distribution compiler from two years ago answering the phone. Two: binaries go to ~/.cargo/bin, never to /usr/local By default cargo install writes into $CARGO_HOME/bin , which is ~/.cargo/bin — a directory you own. Never prefix it with sudo : root's home is not your home, and the binary you just spent four minutes compiling will be invisible. --root changes the destination; nothing else should. Three: PATH and the compiler are the two things that break A successful install and a command not found mean PATH. A cargo install that dies in a build script means a missing system library or a toolchain that is too old. There is almost no third category — part 05 covers the first, part 16 covers the second. Why "compiled" changes the maintenance story A Python tool breaks when its interpreter moves; a Go tool is one file; a Rust tool is one file too, statically linked against everything except the C library. Copy it to another machine of the same OS and architecture and it runs — no crates, no toolchain, no compiler needed on the target. The cost is paid once, at install time, and it is not small: a first install of a large crate can take minutes. Part 03 is mostly about not paying that cost twice. Four commands that people confuse Command What it does Use it when cargo install crate Compiles the crate's binary targets and copies them into ~/.cargo/bin . Works outside any project. Always, for a tool you want to keep. This is the command of the manual. cargo install --path . Compiles the crate in the current directory from its working tree. You are developing that tool, or testing a patch before proposing it. cargo binstall crate Downloads a prebuilt binary from the project's releases when one exists, and falls back to cargo install when it does not. You want the tool now and not in six minutes. Part 13 installs binstall itself. cargo add crate Adds a dependency to the current project's Cargo.toml . Puts nothing on your PATH. You are writing Rust code that imports the crate as a library. One nuance that surprises people coming from Go: a crate can be both a library and a binary, and cargo install only cares about the binary targets. Installing ripgrep does not put a library on your system for other programs to use; it puts rg in your PATH. The two lives are separate, which is why an install never disturbs a project that happens to depend on the same crate. 02 The toolchain, from rustup Rust ships as a toolchain manager and three programs. rustup decides which compiler is current; rustc compiles; cargo resolves, builds and installs. A stable release lands every six weeks, and the line at the time of writing is 1.99 — which matters, because several crates in part 06 ask for 1.95 or newer and cannot be built by anything older. Linux and macOS, the official way curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh # it asks one question; the default profile is right for a workstation # 1) Proceed with standard installation source "$HOME/.cargo/env" # or open a new terminal rustc --version # rustc 1.99.0 (…) cargo --version # cargo 1.99.0 (…) The script is a shell program you can read before running it, and it writes only inside ~/.cargo and ~/.rustup . Two profiles exist: default adds rustfmt, clippy and the documentation, minimal adds nothing but the compiler — the second is what a CI image wants, because it is half the download. To change later: rustup set profile default , then rustup component add rustfmt clippy . Windows Download rustup-init.exe from rustup.rs. It will offer to install the Visual Studio C++ build tools for you, and you should accept: Rust on Windows links with link.exe , and without it every build fails at the last step with a linker error that mentions no missing package. If you already have Visual Studio with the C++ workload, skip that part. The MSYS2 toolchain is an alternative, not an addition — pick one. The components worth knowing Component What it gives you Install it rustfmt The formatter behind cargo fmt , and the reason Rust code looks the same in every repository. rustup component add rustfmt clippy The linter behind cargo clippy : several hundred checks, most of them about a construct that compiles and should not. rustup component add clippy rust-analyzer The language server your editor talks to. Installing it through rustup keeps it in step with the compiler. rustup component add rust-analyzer rust-src The standard library's source, for reading Option instead of guessing and for some debugger setups. rustup component add rust-src llvm-tools llvm-cov and friends, for coverage and binary inspection. rustup component add llvm-tools Pinning a project to a toolchain A rust-toolchain.toml in the repository root is the honest way to say "this builds with 1.95". rustup reads it when you enter the directory and installs that toolchain if it is missing; nobody has to remember which version the project wanted. # rust-toolchain.toml [toolchain] channel = "1.95.0" components = ["rustfmt", "clippy"] # or, for a one-off directory you do not want to commit rustup override set 1.95.0 rustup override unset # what is installed, and which one is answering rustup show rustup toolchain list Prefer channel = "1.95.0" to "stable" for anything you will come back to: stable moves under you six weeks at a time, which is fine for a program and unkind to a build that has to reproduce. Nightly exists for unstable features and is a legitimate answer only when a crate says so in its README. The distribution package, and why it is a trap here Debian, Fedora and Arch all package rustc and cargo . They work, they are fast to install, and they are usually several releases behind — which is exactly the failure mode of part 06, where eight crates declare an MSRV above 1.90. Worse, if both exist, your shell may run the distribution cargo while your ~/.cargo/bin holds another, and the error messages will not tell you which. Either use rustup, or use the distribution package and never mix; do not install both and hope. 03 cargo install: the whole installation story One command, one register, one destination. cargo install ripgrep resolves the newest compatible version of the crate, downloads it and its dependency tree, compiles everything in release mode, and copies the resulting executables into ~/.cargo/bin . There is no resolver choosing a version for you beyond "newest that fits", no environment to activate, and no record to consult afterwards except cargo install --list . The command, with the flag that matters cargo install --locked ripgrep rg --version --locked is not decoration. Without it, Cargo is allowed to update the versions of dependencies to the newest semver-compatible ones, which is how a tool that compiled for everyone else fails on your machine because a transitive crate published a minor release an hour ago. With it, Cargo uses the Cargo.lock the author tested. Almost every project in part 06 publishes a lock file for exactly this reason, and the manual always passes the flag. The flags worth memorising Flag What it does --locked Uses the crate's Cargo.lock exactly. Fewer surprises, occasionally an older dependency than you expected. --version 15.2.0 Pins the crate. The value is the registry version without a v , unlike Go's tags. --root ~/.local Writes to ~/.local/bin instead of ~/.cargo/bin . Useful when that directory is already on PATH. --git https://… Builds from a repository instead of the registry, at the default branch unless --branch or --tag is added. --no-default-features Compiles without the crate's default feature set — fewer dependencies, less code, sometimes no GUI or no TLS. --features git Adds a named feature. Read the crate's README before guessing: feature names are the crate's own vocabulary. --force Overwrites an existing binary. Needed when two crates ship a target with the same name, or when you reinstall the same version. --list / --root Lists what cargo installed and where. The only inventory you have. Pin, or float cargo install crate always takes the newest published version; there is no @latest to argue about. Pin when the tool is part of a pipeline — a formatter in CI, a linter in a hook, a test runner that defines what "passing" means. Float when the tool's job is to track a moving target, and reinstall monthly. Either way, write the version down somewhere outside your shell history; the builder in part 06 does it for you. Upgrading, and the tool that upgrades everything cargo install --locked ripgrep # newest, over the old binary cargo install --list # what is here, with versions cargo uninstall ripgrep # remove the binary, keep the cache # cargo-update adds the missing verb cargo install --locked cargo-update cargo install-update --all Rust has no equivalent of Go's "download a toolchain because the module asked". The compiler you have is the compiler that compiles, and a crate that requires more fails with a clear message naming the version. That is why the check below exists: it answers, before a four-minute build, whether the crates you picked are inside your compiler's reach. Check the MSRV before you compile Each crate may declare a minimum supported Rust version in its published metadata. It is a promise, not a guess: below it the crate is not expected to build, and above it the author has agreed not to raise the floor without a semver-minor release. It is fast because it is compiled and because it only asks the modules the current directory can use. The reason to choose it over a hand-written prompt is not beauty; it is that a new language gets supported by an upgrade instead of by editing your .bashrc . cargo install --locked starship # ~/.bashrc, or the zsh / fish equivalent eval "$(starship init bash)" eval "$(starship init zsh)" # a minimal prompt, in ~/.config/starship.toml add_newline = false [character] success_symbol = "[\$](bold green)" error_symbol = "[\$](bold red)" [git_branch] format = "on [\$branch](\$style) " zoxide — cd, but it remembers It keeps a score for every directory you visit and lets you jump by fragment: z proj from anywhere. The ranking is what makes it work — frequency and recency, not a list you maintain. Hook it over cd with --cmd cd and it behaves like cd for paths that exist, and like a jump for anything else, which is the version people keep. cargo install --locked zoxide eval "$(zoxide init bash --cmd cd)" # zsh / fish / nushell too z blog # best match for "blog" z blog docs # both fragments, any order zi # pick interactively (needs fzf or skim) zoxide query -ls # the whole ranking, with scores atuin — history as a database Your shell history is a flat file that every terminal writes to at exit, which is why it loses commands, duplicates others and cannot tell you what failed. LEVEL 00 BRIEFING From an empty shell to a shipped terminal program This is a linear manual for building terminal user interfaces in Rust: not “hello, world” with colours, but a real program with state, input, tests, an audit trail and a release artefact. Each level ends in a field check, and the next level stays locked until you pass it. That is deliberate: every later level assumes the vocabulary of the one before, and TUIs fail precisely where people skip the fundamentals — terminal state, input parsing, and the borrow checker. Read time ~12 min Prerequisite none Field check 4 questions · 80% Toolchain Rust 1.99.x stable 0.1 Why Rust, and why a terminal A terminal program is a small graphics engine made of bytes. You write escape sequences into a file descriptor, and an emulator somewhere downstream turns those bytes into a grid of cells. Everything people find hard about the genre — flicker, torn layouts, keys that arrive three frames late, menus that leave ghosts behind — has a mechanical cause, and Rust is unusually good at making those causes visible instead of accidental. Rust earns its place in a TUI for concrete reasons, not fashion: No garbage collector in the frame budget. A collector can pause at any point; a 16 ms frame budget has no room for “any point”. Rust's ownership model gives deterministic destruction instead. One self-contained binary. A user downloads one file, runs it, and gets a UI. No runtime, no node_modules, no interpreter version lottery. This matters more for CLI tools than for web apps, because distribution is the product. Parsing untrusted text safely. TUIs are text pipelines: logs, filenames, JSON from an API, clipboard paste. Rust removes whole classes of memory bugs from the code that handles that text, while still requiring you to sanitise control sequences (Level 08). Algebraic data types for UI state. A TUI is a state machine. enum Mode { Browse, Filter, Confirm(ConfirmKind) } plus exhaustive match makes “impossible” screens actually impossible, instead of a boolean soup that drifts out of sync. Errors are values. Result forces you to decide what a failed terminal write means. In a UI that must restore the user's terminal, that decision is the difference between a clean exit and a broken shell. Cargo. Reproducible builds, a lockfile, feature flags, a test runner, a doc builder and a linter — one tool, one file, thirty years of build-system scar tissue avoided. The honest costs A manual that only sells is a brochure. Rust costs you real time in this domain: Fit check — be honest before you commit Rust is a good fit when… Rust is a poor fit when… You ship a single binary to many machines You need a prototype this afternoon and will throw it away The UI owns long-lived state and untrusted input You want a rich widget gallery with batteries included Startup time and memory matter (embedded, SSH, containers) You need hot reload of layout and instant iteration You can afford a slower first week for fewer late bugs Your team already knows TypeScript and the tool is internal You care about cross-compiling to musl, ARM, Windows You mostly need charts and will render them in a browser anyway Compile times are the tax. A ratatui binary with a modest dependency tree takes noticeably longer to link than a Python script takes to start — and you will feel it in the edit–run loop. Levels 01, 02 and 07 are largely about reducing that tax with cargo check , mold / lld , sccache , split debug info and a disciplined dependency policy. The borrow checker is the other tax, and Level 03 is a targeted course in not fighting it: most “borrow checker problems” in TUIs are actually state-modelling problems. Terminology TUI (text user interface) draws into the terminal's cell grid and reads keys; CLI is line-oriented input/output; GUI owns a window. A TUI can be full-screen or inline. This manual builds a full-screen, alternate-screen application, and Level 09 adds a non-interactive mode so the same binary behaves in pipes and CI. 0.2 What Rust actually is, in one page Rust is a statically typed, ahead-of-time compiled language with no garbage collector. Memory is managed by ownership : every value has exactly one owner, moves are explicit, and borrows are checked at compile time. That single rule cascades into the rest of the language's personality. Affine types. A value can be moved once and dropped once. Using a moved value is a compile error, which is why “use after free” is not a runtime category here. Enums are sum types. Option<T> and Result<T, E> are ordinary library enums; null and exceptions are not special cases in the type system. Traits, not inheritance. Behaviour is described by traits and implemented per type; dispatch is static unless you ask for dyn . Editions. The language evolves in opt-in editions (2015, 2018, 2021, 2024) while one compiler keeps compiling all of them. “Edition 2024” is a dialect, not a toolchain version. Zero-cost abstractions is a goal, not a promise. Iterators usually compile to the same machine code as a loop; Box<dyn Trait> , Rc , and excessive clone() do not. Measure (Level 07). Unsafe is a boundary, not a mode. unsafe unlocks five specific capabilities (raw pointers, FFI, unions, mutable statics, unsafe trait impls). The rest of the language does not change. Three slogans, translated Marketing versus mechanics Slogan What it really means Where it fails “Fearless concurrency” Data races are compile errors; Send / Sync encode thread-safety in types Deadlocks, starvation and logical races are still yours “If it compiles, it works” Whole bug classes are eliminated before runtime Layout bugs, wrong colours, bad UX and unwrap() panics all compile “Zero-cost abstractions” Many high-level constructs lower to tight code Allocation, dynamic dispatch and cloning are not free; profile Hold on to that third column. Every level of this manual has a BAD DECISION block, because the fastest way to learn a systems language is to study the failure modes people actually ship. 0.3 The artefact you will build: tuitop Everything in this manual points at one program. tuitop is a process and system monitor for the terminal: a sortable process table, a detail pane, live sparklines, a filter prompt, a command palette, a help overlay, a config file, a non-interactive --once mode, tests and a release pipeline. It is deliberately not a todo list, because a monitor has the properties that make TUIs hard and therefore teach the right lessons: Continuous data that arrives from a worker thread while the UI stays responsive (Level 05). Untrusted strings from process names, command lines and log files (Levels 04 and 08). Dense layout with tables, tabs, gauges and popups that must survive a 40×10 terminal (Level 06). Real failure modes : permission denied, a process vanishing between read and render, a terminal that lies about its colour support. Target shape by the end of Level 10: The split is not ceremony. Keeping tuitop-core free of terminal types is what makes it testable without a TTY, and it is the difference between a UI you can refactor and one you can only poke at. The rule is simple: domain logic never imports a rendering crate. 0.4 How the gating works Each level is one page. At the bottom sits a sealed field check . A note on honesty The questions are written to test judgement , not trivia. Several have more than one defensible answer in the real world; the explanation says why one is preferred here. Bad decision 0.A Making a TUI your very first Rust program It is a tempting first project because it is visible : you get a screen, colours and keypresses in an hour, instead of a guessing game. The trouble is that a TUI stacks four independent difficulty curves on top of each other — ownership and lifetimes, terminal protocol/state, layout arithmetic, and async or threading for live data. When it breaks you cannot tell which curve broke, so you debug all four at once, and most people conclude “Rust is too hard” when the truth is “the project was four projects”. Why it tempts Immediate visual feedback; tutorials promise a working dashboard in 60 lines; it feels like a real program. What breaks Borrow errors are blamed on the terminal, terminal corruption is blamed on Rust, and the project is abandoned around the first resize bug. Do instead Read the Book through chapter 8 and do rustlings while working through Level 03. Then build the TUI with each layer isolated — domain logic first, rendering second. LEVEL 01 TOOLCHAIN Install once, configure deliberately Most “Rust is broken” reports are installation reports. A stale distribution rustc , a half-installed toolchain without clippy , a PATH that works in your terminal but not in your editor, or a global RUSTFLAGS that silently invalidates every cache. This level installs the compiler through the only supported channel, then configures the four files that shape the rest of your project. Read time ~22 min Prerequisite Level 00 Field check 5 questions · 80% Toolchain rustup + stable 1.99.x 1.1 What rustup actually manages rustup is a toolchain multiplexer, not an installer that happens to also update. It owns four things, and understanding them prevents most confusion: Toolchains. A toolchain is a matched set: rustc , cargo , rust-std for your targets, rustdoc , and optionally clippy , rustfmt , rust-src . stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu is one toolchain; nightly-2026-10-01 is another. They live side by side under ~/.rustup/toolchains/ . Components. Optional pieces attached to a toolchain: clippy , rustfmt , rust-src (for rust-analyzer and cargo doc internals), rust-analyzer , llvm-tools (for coverage and profiling), miri (nightly only). Targets. Cross-compilation standard libraries, e.g. x86_64-unknown-linux-musl , aarch64-apple-darwin , x86_64-pc-windows-msvc . Installing a target gives you libstd ; it does not give you a linker or a sysroot, which is why cross-compilation still needs help (§9.3). Proxies. The rustc , cargo , rustdoc and rustfmt binaries in ~/.cargo/bin are tiny shims that read your override settings and exec the right toolchain. That is why cargo +nightly works and why your PATH order matters more than which binary you think you called. Two directories, two jobs ~/.rustup holds toolchains and the rustup settings. ~/.cargo holds your binaries ( ~/.cargo/bin , where cargo install puts things) and configuration ( ~/.cargo/config.toml ). Backing up ~/.cargo alone does not back up Rust; deleting ~/.rustup removes every toolchain. 1.2 Installing on each platform Linux and macOS — the official script The one-liner curl … | sh is the same thing with one fewer chance to inspect it. In a regulated environment, download the script, pin its SHA-256 in your provisioning code, and verify before executing. The script installs rustup into ~/.cargo/bin and ~/.rustup ; nothing goes into /usr/local , and no root is required. Windows Download and run rustup-init.exe from rustup.rs . The default host triple is x86_64-pc-windows-msvc , which needs the Visual Studio Build Tools with the “Desktop development with C++” workload and a Windows SDK — this supplies link.exe . Without it you get linker `link.exe` not found . If you cannot install MSVC, the alternative host is x86_64-pc-windows-gnu , which brings its own MinGW linker but produces a binary that depends on MinGW runtime DLLs unless you link statically. For scripted Windows installs (CI, images), the same rustup-init.exe accepts the flags: Verify — and read the output If rustup show reports a toolchain you did not expect, check for an override: rustup override list shows per-directory pins, and a rust-toolchain.toml in a parent directory silently wins (§1.4). 1.3 Post-install configuration that pays for itself 1. PATH, for every process that is not your shell The installer appends . "$HOME/.cargo/env" to your shell profile. Interactive shells then find cargo . Your editor, your IDE's language server and your desktop-launched GUI may not read that file. On Linux, log-in shells read ~/.profile while interactive non-login shells read ~/.bashrc ; put the PATH export in ~/.profile (or ~/.config/environment.d/rust.conf on systemd systems) so GUI sessions inherit it too: On macOS, GUI apps read a different environment than your shell; if rust-analyzer is not found by VS Code, launch the editor from a terminal once to confirm, or set the server path explicitly. On Windows the installer edits your user PATH ; terminals already open keep the old one, so restart them before concluding the install failed. 2. Components — install the whole working set up front rust-src is not optional if you use rust-analyzer 's “go to definition” into the standard library, and it is required by cargo miri . llvm-tools supplies llvm-profdata / llvm-cov for cargo llvm-cov . rust-analyzer as a rustup component keeps the server version matched to the compiler instead of drifting with an extension update. 3. ~/.cargo/config.toml — global defaults, deliberately few Cargo merges configuration from the current directory upward, then ~/.cargo/config.toml , with environment variables on top. Keep the global file small; project-specific settings belong in the repository. Where not to put things Do not set a global target-dir unless you have measured a problem it solves: it forces every project to share one directory, which serialises builds and confuses tooling that expects ./target . Do not set [build] rustflags or a global RUSTFLAGS environment variable for flags you only need in one project — see Bad decision 1.C. 4. Pin the toolchain in the repository A rust-toolchain.toml at the project root makes rustup install and select exactly this toolchain for anyone who enters the directory, on any machine, including CI. This is the single highest-value configuration file in a Rust repository. Pin exactly for applications you ship; a range such as channel = "stable" is friendlier for libraries, where CI should test the MSRV and the latest stable instead of freezing one. Either way, write rust-version in Cargo.toml so the resolver and your users know the floor (Level 02). 1.4 Channels, overrides and the nightly question Toolchain selection, in precedence order Mechanism Command / file Scope Use it for CLI override cargo +nightly run one command Trying a nightly-only flag or Miri Environment RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.99.1 one process tree CI jobs, build scripts Directory override rustup override set nightly this directory Temporary, local experiments Toolchain file rust-toolchain.toml directory tree The committed, reproducible choice Default rustup default stable user Everything else Channels are stable (released every six weeks), beta (the next stable, branched six weeks ahead) and nightly (built daily, no stability guarantees). A dated nightly, nightly-2026-10-01 , is reproducible; the floating nightly is not, and a build that works today can fail tomorrow for reasons unrelated to your code. Use nightly for exactly three things in this manual: Miri (undefined-behaviour detection in tests), sanitizers and coverage edge cases that need -Z flags, and occasionally cargo udeps for unused dependencies. Nothing you ship should require nightly. There is no “nightly feature” worth a broken release pipeline for a TUI. 1.5 Make the edit–run loop survivable Rust's compile time is the main daily friction, and three settings remove most of it without touching your code: cargo check instead of cargo build during design. Type-checking without codegen is typically several times faster and catches the errors you actually make while structuring a program. A faster linker. Link time dominates incremental rebuilds of a TUI with a real dependency tree. lld or mold on Linux, lld via zld /default on macOS, and lld-link on Windows all help. A compiler cache. sccache or cargo-cache for artefacts; sccache also shares across branches and CI. These flags only affect the host target and only link the final binary. That distinction matters: rustflags changes Cargo's fingerprint, so switching them invalidates cached builds. Keep them in the project, commit the file, and let everyone share the same cache key. seFosseDitador: Se Eu fosse um Ditador Estrutura Global do Manifesto Introdução: O Paradoxo do Poder Absoluto e a Necessidade de Reforma Capítulo I: O Fim da Pobreza Extrema e a Reestruturação Económica Capítulo II: A Revolução Educativa e o Cultivo do Pensamento Crítico Capítulo III: Sustentabilidade e Emergência Climática Capítulo IV: Justiça, Direitos Humanos e Governação Global Capítulo V: Ciência, Tecnologia e Transição Energética Conclusão: O Legado da Transição e o Regresso à Governação Partilhada O Paradoxo do Poder Absoluto e a Necessidade de Reforma PARTE 1: A GÉNESE DO PODER ABSOLUTO E A NATUREZA DA CRISE GLOBAL O Dilema do Arquitecto Absoluto Assumir a premissa de um poder autocrático planetário é ingressar num dos campos mais perigosos e complexos da filosofia política. Ao longo da história humana, a figura do ditador, designada originalmente na República Romana como uma magistratura extraordinária, temporária e constitucional para responder a emergências extremas, degenerou, quase invariavelmente, em despotismo, tirania e megalomania. A concentração de autoridade absoluta nas mãos de um único indivíduo ou de uma junta restrita constitui uma tentação corrosiva, onde os mecanismos de controlo, a capacidade de empatia e o discernimento ético tendem a ser esmagados pela soberba do comando. No entanto, a proposição do presente ensaio não nasce do desejo narcísico de dominação ou da fantasia pueril de controlo social. Pelo contrário, surge de um diagnóstico sóbrio, doloroso e inadiável sobre o estado do mundo contemporâneo. Vivemos numa era caracterizada pela paralisia das democracias liberais diante de crises sistémicas globais, pela incapacidade do multilateralismo internacional em travar guerras desumanas, pelo crescimento descontrolado da desigualdade socioeconómica e pela aceleração vertiginosa do colapso ecológico. Quando os mecanismos normais de governação, caracterizados pela burocracia lenta, pelos interesses de lobbies financeiros e pela polarização partidária de curto prazo, se mostram impotentes para resolver problemas que ameaçam a própria sobrevivência da espécie humana, surge o dilema do "autocrata benevolente". Pode o poder absoluto, se exercido com rigor ético, clareza filosófica e um plano de desmantelamento programado, servir como o bisturi necessário para amputar as gangrenas da civilização moderna? A resposta a esta questão exige um paradoxo fundamental: para que um poder absoluto seja genuinamente ético, a sua primeira e maior prioridade deve ser a criação de condições para a sua própria extinção. O "Ditador Benevolente", nesta formulação, não é um governante perpétuo, mas sim um arquiteto de transição. É um agente temporário investido de força executiva ilimitada, cujo objetivo final não é a manutenção do controlo, mas o estabelecimento de uma nova ordem justa, sustentável e descentralizada, capaz de ser gerida democraticamente por gerações futuras. II. A Falência do Diagnóstico Contemporâneo e a Paralisia Multilateral Para compreender a necessidade de uma reforma radical e sem precedentes, é preciso examinar as falhas estruturais das instituições globais do século XXI. O sistema internacional fundado no pós-Segunda Guerra Mundial, consubstanciado na Organização das Nações Unidas, nas instituições de Bretton Woods e no direito internacional público, colapsou na sua capacidade operativa. O direito de veto do Conselho de Segurança da ONU transforma a justiça internacional num espetáculo de seletividade geopolítica. Conflitos armados devastam regiões inteiras, genocídios velados e explícitos desdobram-se em tempo real nas ecrãs dos nossos telefones, e as potências mundiais utilizam a diplomacia não como uma ferramenta de paz, mas como um escudo para proteger os seus interesses geestratégicos e as suas indústrias de armamento. O multilateralismo converteu-se numa assembleia de conversações estéreis, onde resoluções são votadas sem poder de execução e onde os direitos humanos são proclamados em papel enquanto são violados na prática. Simultaneamente, o sistema económico global hipercapitalista opera de forma desvinculada dos limites biológicos do planeta e do bem-estar social. A acumulação desmedida de capital nas mãos de uma fração ínfima da população global contrasta obscenamente com a pobreza extrema de milhares de milhões de seres humanos que carecem de água potável, saneamento, alimentação adequada e cuidados de saúde elementares. Os mercados financeiros, impulsionados pela especulação de curto prazo e por algoritmos opacos, ditam as políticas públicas de nações soberanas, forçando governos democraticamente eleitos a desmantelar sistemas de proteção social em nome de uma austeridade sufocante. Paralelamente, a crise climática deixou de ser uma previsão do futuro para se tornar uma realidade devastadora no presente. As emissões de gases de efeito de estufa continuam a aumentar, as florestas tropicais são destruídas a taxas alarmantes, a biodiversidade do planeta está a sofrer a sexta extinção em massa e os oceanos estão a acidificar-se e a encher-se de plástico. As cimeiras do clima (COPs) sucedem-se ano após ano, produzindo acordos não vinculativos, promessas vazias e metas adiadas para datas distantes, enquanto a janela de oportunidade para evitar pontos de rutura irreversíveis se fecha rapidamente. Diante desta tripla crise geopolítica, económica e ecológica, a democracia representativa tradicional viu-se capturada por ciclos eleitorais de quatro ou cinco anos. Os líderes políticos raramente pensam além da próxima eleição; são reféns da opinião pública moldada pela desinformação das redes sociais, financiados por grandes corporações e temerosos de adotar as medidas impopulares, porém vitais, que a longo prazo salvariam a civilização. É neste cenário de paralisia sistémica que a ideia de uma intervenção radical ganha força conceptual. Se a casa comum está a arder e os moradores discutem proceduralmente quem deve segurar a mangueira enquanto a estrutura desaba, torna-se necessário um ato de autoridade decisiva para apagar o fogo, retirar os ocupantes do perigo e reconstruir a fundação sobre bases inteiramente novas. III. A Filosofia do Poder Consciente: Ética e Limites da Vontade A premissa "Se eu fosse um Ditador" pressupõe uma profunda responsabilidade filosófica. O exercício do poder sem uma doutrina ética explícita degenera inevitavelmente na tirania. Portanto, o exercício desta autoridade absoluta deve ser balizado por princípios inegociáveis que diferenciam a reforma benevolente da opressão despótica. O primeiro princípio é a Soberania do Bem Comum. O poder não pertence ao ditador; o ditador é meramente o guardião temporário da soberania coletiva da humanidade. Todas as decisões, decretos e reestruturações devem responder estritamente à pergunta: "Esta medida reduz o sofrimento humano, protege a biosfera e promove o desenvolvimento integral das capacidades da civilização?" Se a resposta for negativa, a medida é ilegítima, independentemente da conveniência política. O segundo princípio é o da Nobreza dos Meios e dos Fins. Historicamente, os regimes autoritários justificaram atrocidades sob o lema de que "os fins justificam os meios". O nosso manifesto rejeita categoricamente esta máxima. Uma reforma que busque a paz global não pode ser edificada sobre o purgo em massa ou a eliminação física de dissidentes. A força exercida por esta ditadura temporária deve ser primariamente institucional, jurídica, económica e estrutural desmantelando privilégios, monopólios e armas de destruição massiva, e não violentando a integridade física e a dignidade fundamental dos cidadãos. O terceiro princípio é a Transparência Absoluta e a Racionalidade Científica. Na era da informação, um poder benevolente não opera nas sombras de gabinetes secretos, mas sob a luz pública. Todas as decisões executivas devem ser fundamentadas em evidências científicas rigorosas, dados abertos e consultas públicas a especialistas independentes, filósofos, cientistas, líderes comunitários e representantes dos povos originários. O dogma ideológico deve ser substituído pelo pragmatismo humanista. O quarto e mais crucial princípio é a Autolimitação e a Cláusula de Extinção. Uma ditadura que não planeia o seu próprio fim é uma tirania em gestação. Desde o primeiro dia de governação, deve ser promulgado uma "Constituição de Transição Global", na qual se estipula de forma clara, mensurável e irrevogável o cronograma para a devolução do poder. A ditadura terminará quando os objetivos fundamentais da reforma erradicação da pobreza extrema, desarmamento global completo, estabilização climática inicial e instituição de um novo sistema democrático multinível forem alcançados.
